For most iPhone owners, I'd pick the **Anker Prime Qi2 25W vent mount**. If you want something cheaper, the **ESR HaloLock CryoBoost** is the best value. Prices below come from the guides and may have changed.

**Top picks**
- **Best overall: [Anker Prime Qi2 car mount](https://amzn.to/4vhoGXa)** (about $70–90).
  - MountGuys uses it daily in its own car and calls it the best overall pick. It does up to 25W and has active cooling.
  - It comes with a 60W car adapter, and the clip grips vents more securely than Apple's or Belkin's mounts.
  - The Gadgeteer says its vent clip is narrow, so check your vent slat width first.
- **Best value with a fan: [ESR HaloLock Qi2 with CryoBoost](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CM3DCWQY?tag=r3media07-20)** (15W, fan-cooled).
  - It doesn't include a car adapter, so budget $10–15 for one.
  - The Gadgeteer lists its price as both $18.99 and $35.99, so check the current price on the listing.
- **Best 25W with adapter: [LISEN Qi2.2 25W with cooling fan](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FPFH7BN9?tag=r3media07-20)** (about $40).
  - It's The Gadgeteer's top pick, and a 95W adapter is included.
  - It only reaches 25W with the fan on.
  - I found no hands-on testing for it beyond that review.
- **Cheapest Qi2 option: [ESR HaloLock Qi2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08HNBHSQV?tag=r3media07-20)** (about $20–27).
  - It has no active cooling and no adapter.
  - It's fine if your car stays cool.

**Other situations**
- **Eye-level dash or windshield:** the [iOttie Velox Mini Qi2](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D54Y5THX?tag=r3media07-20) (15W, charger included, about $42). MountGuys prefers the non-charging [Andobil suction mount](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FWJYCJC6?tag=moun05-20). Windshield mounts are restricted in some states, including California, Minnesota and New Jersey.
- **Trucks or rough roads:** the [RAM Drill Down](https://amzn.to/3O2iQZj) bolts into the dash. It's the most stable option, but it needs drilling, so it's a poor fit for leased cars.
- **No usable vent or dash space:** the [EXELIQ cup holder mount](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0BJ688W1Q/?tag=moun05-20) (15W).
- **No charging, just a secure hold:** the [VICSEED steel-core vent mount](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0F916XVSW/?tag=moun05-20).

**Before you buy**
- **Look for the Qi2 badge.** "MagSafe-compatible" without Qi2 certification may charge at only about 7.5W.
- **You need a proper car adapter.** Car USB ports usually can't deliver enough power. A 15W mount needs an adapter of at least 18W. A 25W mount needs 30W or more.
- **The guides disagree on Anker's adapter requirement.** The Gadgeteer says 45W or higher, and MountGuys says 60W. The included 60W adapter covers both.
- **Heat matters.** Passive mounts can throttle in direct sun. The Gadgeteer says they can drop to about 7W. A fan-cooled or TEC-cooled mount avoids this.
- **Use a MagSafe case.** A plain case weakens the magnet hold.

**Caveats**
- The Gadgeteer's list has some price inconsistencies, and MountGuys has only hands-on tested the Anker and Andobil.
- I couldn't read the WIRED roundup because the page was too large for my tools to open.
- One search result lists a PARTNER18 code for $7.19 off the [ESR HaloLock 15W Wireless Car Charger with CryoBoost](https://dealectric.com/lab/V8/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost) on ESR's store. That's the CryoBoost model, and the page says it was tested on 2026-10-22. I didn't open that page, so confirm the code at checkout.

Tell me your iPhone model, where you want to mount it and your budget, and I can narrow this to one pick.

 After testing different mounting styles across a wide range of vehicles, from compact sedans to larger trucks, the best MagSafe car mounts come down to three things: mount stability, magnet strength, and placement.
